en.title: Reflexive verbs
en.summary: English uses -self pronouns for reflexive actions, but less often than other languages.

paragraphs: A reflexive verb has an object pronoun that refers back to the subject: I hurt myself. In many languages such verbs are very common, but English uses the reflexive pronoun much less.

items: She **taught herself** to play the guitar.

sections.title: Verbs that need a reflexive pronoun

blocks.html:
VerbExample
enjoy oneselfWe enjoyed ourselves.
behave yourselfBehave yourself!
help yourselfHelp yourself to the cake.
hurt / cut / burn oneselfHe cut himself shaving.
introduce oneselfShe introduced herself.
teach oneselfI taught myself Spanish.

sections.title: Verbs that do not take a reflexive in English

paragraphs: Verbs of grooming, such as wash, dress, shave and get up, do not normally take a reflexive pronoun when the meaning is obvious. Use the reflexive for emphasis, or when a person is not able to do it: He dressed himself (even though he is only three).

blocks.html:
EnglishNot
She washed and dressed.She washed herself and dressed herself.
I shave every day.I shave myself every day.
We relaxed.We relaxed ourselves.
He hurried.He hurried himself.

items: After a preposition when it refers to the subject: **He talked to himself.**
Do not use for different people: **They saw them** (different people) vs **They saw themselves.**
Wrong: **I feel myself tired.** Right: **I feel tired.**
Wrong: **He sat himself down.** Right: **He sat down.**
